newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N.'s Ekeus escalating tension with Iraq - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Ekeus escalating tension with Iraq - paper.

text.p: An official Iraqi newspaper on Tuesday accused top U.N. arms inspector Rolf Ekeus of "aggressive remarks" and attempts to escalate tensions with Iraq.
"Ekeus made late in January one of his most aggressive statements, exposing his impartiality and lost of independence," al-Iraq said in a commentary.

Ekeus last month was reported to have told a Washington think-tank that weakly worded statements by the U.N. Security Council encouraged Iraq to obstruct efforts by his arms experts to scrap Baghdad's weapons of mass destruction.

Ekeus heads the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) disarming Iraq under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire. He is due in Baghdad on February 20 in his latest bid to defuse a stand-off over wrecked missile parts which his commission would like to take abroad for analysis.

"Such stands from UNSCOM's chairman no longer surprise us. But what really stirs our anger is the fact that the criminal embargo continues because his commission is not subjective and independent," al-Iraq said.

Sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait can be lifted only when Ekeus's commission decides that Iraq has scrapped all of its weapons of mass destruction including missiles with ranges greater than 150 km (93 miles).

A U.N. ballistic missile team is in Baghdad examining excavations by Iraq of its missile sites. More than 100 wrecked missiles engines have been uncovered so far but UNSCOM, expressing doubts about their authenticity, insists on having them analysed in the United States.
